title: Floating Sliding Door
description:
A sliding glass door with no visible track at the head or the floor, so the panel appears to float. It was developed with a European hardware partner for offices, homes and hospitality, at a lower price and with an easier installation than CRL's existing commercial sliders.

I took over the program at Gate 3. Before committing to inventory we surveyed architects on the concept: 85% found it appealing and 77% said they were likely to specify it. Their comments shaped the launch messaging around minimal hardware and clean lines.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: Customers want contemporary sliding doors that are affordable and simple to install.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: A concealed-track sliding system for residential and commercial use, as a lighter-duty alternative to CRL's 690/695 sliders.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects, for the aesthetics; contractors, for the cost and ease of installation. Offices, residential and hospitality.

brief.label: Value
brief.text: No visible track or bottom guide, concealed hardware, and an accessible price.

brief.label: Sourcing
brief.text: Buy: developed with an existing European hardware partner.

brief.label: Competition
brief.text: Milcasa and Qiwin; Home Depot and Amazon barn doors in wood at the low end.
